protocolBuilder.interface.geospatial.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for locating network members on a map. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.information.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for presenting researcher-authored information. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.nameGenerator.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for naming network members using forms. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.nameGeneratorQ.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for quickly naming network members. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.nameGeneratorR.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for selecting network members from roster data. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.narrative.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for recording a narrative. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.narrativePedig.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface combining a narrative with a family genealogy. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.networkCompose.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for building and editing a network. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.oneToManyDyadC.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for asking about one network member's relationships with several others. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.ordinalBin.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for arranging network members in ordered categories. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.sociogram.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for drawing and arranging a network. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interface.tieStrengthCen.description: Researcher-facing interface name. Interface for reporting the strength of relationships between network members. Not a protocol-authored stage label.

protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.clea.description: Action that confirms switching the interviewer guidance off and discarding what was written in it.

protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.clea.defaultMessage: This will clear your interview script, and delete content you previously entered. Do you want to continue?
protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.clea.description: Body of the confirmation asked before switching the interviewer guidance off, which throws away everything the researcher wrote in it.

protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.clea.defaultMessage: This will clear your interview script
protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.clea.description: Title of the confirmation asked before switching the interviewer guidance off, which throws away everything the researcher wrote in it.

protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.desc.defaultMessage: Create notes or a guide for the interviewer.
protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.desc.description: Description of the section holding notes written for the person running the interview.

protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.fiel.description: Label of the rich-text field holding the notes the person running the interview reads while this step runs.

protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.plac.defaultMessage: Enter text for the interviewer here...
protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.plac.description: Placeholder of the rich-text field holding the notes the person running the interview reads while this step runs.

protocolBuilder.interviewerGuidance.titl.description: Heading of the section holding notes written for the person running the interview. Never shown to a participant.

protocolBuilder.introduction.description.defaultMessage: Introduce this task to the participant before they start it.

protocolBuilder.introduction.headingHint.defaultMessage: The heading shown at the top of the introduction screen.

protocolBuilder.introduction.headingLabe.description: Label of the field holding the heading at the top of the introduction screen a participant reads.

protocolBuilder.introduction.headingPlac.description: Placeholder shown in the empty introduction-heading field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.introduction.textHint.defaultMessage: Explain what the participant is about to do. This is the only thing they will read before the task begins.

protocolBuilder.introduction.textLabel.description: Label of the field holding the prose a participant reads before this step of the interview begins.

protocolBuilder.introduction.textPlaceho.description: Placeholder shown in the empty introduction-text field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.introduction.title.description: Heading of the section where a researcher writes what a participant reads before this step of the interview begins.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.emptyState.description: Shown in place of the rows when a list has none, and the list’s caller has offered no wording of its own.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.incompleteRo.defaultMessage: Every row needs a value in each column.
protocolBuilder.multiSelect.incompleteRo.description: Shown above a list of rows in a stage editor when the researcher tries to save with a row that has an empty cell in it. Each row here is a set of dropdowns filled in together — a sort rule, a display property.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.removeItem.description: Action that deletes one row of a list. Used as the button on the row, as the title of the confirmation it raises, and as that confirmation’s own confirm button.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.removeItemDe.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to remove this item?
protocolBuilder.multiSelect.removeItemDe.description: Body of the confirmation raised when a researcher deletes one row of a list.

protocolBuilder.multiSelect.reorderItem.description: Accessible name of the handle that drags one row of a list into a different position. position is the row’s own place in the list, counting from one; count is how many rows the list holds.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.clearConfi.description: Action that confirms switching the stage filter off and discarding its rules.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.clearDescr.defaultMessage: This will clear your filter, and delete any rules you have created. Do you want to continue?
protocolBuilder.networkFilter.clearDescr.description: Body of the confirmation asked before switching the stage filter off, which throws away every rule in it.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.clearTitle.description: Title of the confirmation asked before switching the stage filter off, which throws away every rule in it.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.edgeDescri.defaultMessage: Create rules that limit which edges are available on this stage.
protocolBuilder.networkFilter.edgeDescri.description: Description of the stage-filter section on a stage whose filter narrows edges — the relationships between network members.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.edgeRulesH.defaultMessage: Create one or more rules that must match in order for an edge to be shown on this stage.
protocolBuilder.networkFilter.edgeRulesH.description: Guidance under the rule builder on a stage whose filter narrows edges — the relationships between network members.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.hiddenEdge.defaultMessage: This stage creates or displays edges that these rules will not let through, so participants will not see them.
protocolBuilder.networkFilter.hiddenEdge.description: Warning body shown when a stage’s own filter would keep out the edges — the relationships between network members — that the same stage is configured to create or display.
Warning heading shown when a stage’s own filter would keep out the edges — the relationships between network members — that the same stage is configured to create or display.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.nodeDescri.defaultMessage: Create rules that limit which nodes are available on this stage.
protocolBuilder.networkFilter.nodeDescri.description: Description of the stage-filter section on a stage whose filter narrows nodes — the members of the interview network.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.nodeRulesH.defaultMessage: Create one or more rules that must match in order for a node to be shown on this stage.
protocolBuilder.networkFilter.nodeRulesH.description: Guidance under the rule builder on a stage whose filter narrows nodes — the members of the interview network.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.rulesLabel.description: Label of the rule builder inside the stage-filter section, where a researcher writes the rules that decide what reaches the stage.

protocolBuilder.networkFilter.title.description: Heading of the section where a researcher narrows which parts of the interview network one stage works on. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.operators.contains.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute whose text answer matches a regular expression. Read as a whole phrase before the pattern being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.doesNotContain.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute whose text answer does not match a regular expression. Read as a whole phrase before the pattern being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.exactly.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with exactly this value. Read as a whole phrase before the value being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.excludes.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with none of a chosen set of options. Read as a whole phrase before the options being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.exists.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches when the thing being asked about is present in the interview network at all. Compares no value.

protocolBuilder.operators.greaterThan.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with a number above this value. Read as a whole phrase before the value being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.greaterThanOrE.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with a number above this value or equal to it. Read as a whole phrase before the value being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.includes.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with one of a chosen set of options. Read as a whole phrase before the options being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.lessThan.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with a number below this value. Read as a whole phrase before the value being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.lessThanOrEqua.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with a number below this value or equal to it. Read as a whole phrase before the value being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.not.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches an attribute answered with anything other than this value. Read as a whole phrase before the value being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.notExists.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that matches when the thing being asked about is absent from the interview network. Compares no value.

protocolBuilder.operators.optionsEquals.defaultMessage: number of selected options is exactly
protocolBuilder.operators.optionsEquals.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that counts how many options a multiple-choice attribute was answered with and matches exactly this number. Read as a whole phrase before the number being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.optionsGreater.defaultMessage: number of selected options is greater than
protocolBuilder.operators.optionsGreater.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that counts how many options a multiple-choice attribute was answered with and matches a count above this number. Read as a whole phrase before the number being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.optionsLessTha.defaultMessage: number of selected options is less than
protocolBuilder.operators.optionsLessTha.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that counts how many options a multiple-choice attribute was answered with and matches a count below this number. Read as a whole phrase before the number being compared against.

protocolBuilder.operators.optionsNotEqua.defaultMessage: number of selected options is not
protocolBuilder.operators.optionsNotEqua.description: Researcher-facing name for the rule operator that counts how many options a multiple-choice attribute was answered with and matches any count other than this number. Read as a whole phrase before the number being compared against.

protocolBuilder.option.duplicateLabelRow.description: Shown under one option’s label cell when another option in the same list already reads the same way. Terse because it sits inside a row.

protocolBuilder.option.duplicateLabels.defaultMessage: Every option needs a unique label.
protocolBuilder.option.duplicateLabels.description: Shown under a list of options when two of them would read identically to a participant.

protocolBuilder.option.duplicateValueRow.description: Shown under one option’s value cell when another option in the same list is stored as the same answer. Terse because it sits inside a row.

protocolBuilder.option.duplicateValues.defaultMessage: Every option needs a unique value.
protocolBuilder.option.duplicateValues.description: Shown under a list of options when two of them would be stored and exported as the same answer.

protocolBuilder.option.editOption.description: Accessible name of the button that opens one option for editing. position is the option’s own place in the list, counting from one — the only thing that tells two blank options apart.

protocolBuilder.option.emptyState.defaultMessage: No options have been added yet.
protocolBuilder.option.emptyState.description: Shown in place of the list of answers a categorical or ordinal attribute offers, while the researcher has added none.

protocolBuilder.option.finishEditing.description: Accessible name of the button that collapses an option back to a single line once the researcher has filled it in.

protocolBuilder.option.incompleteOptions.defaultMessage: Every option needs both a label and a value.
protocolBuilder.option.incompleteOptions.description: Shown under a list of options when one of them is half-finished. The label is what a participant reads; the value is what the answer is stored and exported as.

protocolBuilder.option.labelLabel.description: Label of the field holding what a participant reads for this option.

protocolBuilder.option.labelPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the empty field holding what a participant reads for this option.

protocolBuilder.option.minimumOptions.defaultMessage: Requires a minimum of two options. If you need fewer options, consider using a boolean attribute.
protocolBuilder.option.minimumOptions.description: Shown under a list of options when the researcher tries to save an ordinal or categorical attribute with fewer than two of them. A boolean attribute is the codebook variable type that records a yes/no answer.

protocolBuilder.option.noValue.description: Stands in for an option’s stored value on the collapsed row while the researcher has not entered one yet.

protocolBuilder.option.optionNoun.description: Noun for one row of the list of options a categorical or ordinal attribute offers. Interpolated mid-sentence into things said ABOUT a row ("This option was replaced…"), so it is lower case and singular.

protocolBuilder.option.removeOption.description: Action that deletes one option from the list. Used as the title of the confirmation it raises and as that confirmation’s own confirm button.

protocolBuilder.option.removeOptionAt.description: Accessible name of the button that deletes one option. position is the option’s own place in the list, counting from one — the only thing that tells two blank options apart.

protocolBuilder.option.removeOptionDescr.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to remove this option?
protocolBuilder.option.removeOptionDescr.description: Body of the confirmation raised when a researcher deletes one option from the list.

protocolBuilder.option.reorderOption.description: Accessible name of the handle that drags one option into a different position. position is the option’s own place in the list, counting from one; count is how many options the list holds.

protocolBuilder.option.untitled.description: Stands in for an option’s label on the collapsed row while the researcher has not written one yet.

protocolBuilder.option.valueLabel.description: Label of the field holding what this option is stored and exported as, as opposed to what a participant reads.

protocolBuilder.option.valuePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the empty field holding what this option is stored and exported as.

protocolBuilder.outline.completeStatus.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: everything it asks for has been filled in and nothing in it is invalid. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

protocolBuilder.outline.errorStatus.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor (a stage is one step of an interview): something the researcher has entered in it is not valid. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen — the same state is drawn as a color and an icon.

protocolBuilder.outline.incompleteStatus.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: it still has required fields the researcher has not filled in. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

protocolBuilder.outline.landmarkLabel.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark listing the sections of the stage being edited. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.outline.statusWithProble.description: Read out for a section of a stage editor whose only account of what is wrong is here. status is the section’s spoken state ("Has a problem"); problems is one or more whole sentences describing what the protocol refused, already in the reader’s language. Both are complete sentences, so this is only the punctuation that separates them.

protocolBuilder.outline.switchedOffStatu.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: the researcher has turned this optional part of the stage off, so it asks for nothing. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

protocolBuilder.outline.unavailableStatu.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: it cannot be filled in until something else in the stage has been chosen. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.atLeastOne.defaultMessage: Add at least one block. A page with no content shows the participant nothing.
protocolBuilder.pageContent.atLeastOne.description: Refusal shown above the list of blocks when a researcher saves a page that shows nothing. A block is one piece of a page — a passage of text, a picture, a video.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.headingHint.defaultMessage: The large heading shown at the top of the page.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.headingLabel.description: Label of the field holding the large heading at the top of a page a participant reads.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.headingPlace.description: Placeholder shown in the empty page-heading field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introAddLabe.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding one more piece to an introduction screen.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introAddTitl.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add one more piece to an introduction screen.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introClearCo.description: Action that confirms switching the introduction screen off and discarding its blocks.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introClearDe.defaultMessage: This will delete every block on the introduction screen, and the participant will start the task straight away. Do you want to continue?
protocolBuilder.pageContent.introClearDe.description: Body of the confirmation asked before switching the introduction screen off, which throws every block on it away.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introClearTi.defaultMessage: This will remove the introduction screen
protocolBuilder.pageContent.introClearTi.description: Title of the confirmation asked before switching the introduction screen off, which throws every block on it away.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introDescrip.defaultMessage: Show the participant a screen of text and media before this task begins.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introEditTit.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a piece of an introduction screen.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introEmptySt.defaultMessage: No blocks yet. Create one to explain this task before the participant starts it.
protocolBuilder.pageContent.introEmptySt.description: Shown in place of the list of blocks while an introduction screen holds nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introItemNou.description: What one piece of an introduction screen is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit introduction block" — so it is lower case and singular.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introItemsHi.defaultMessage: The participant scrolls through these in order before starting the task. Drag to reorder them.
protocolBuilder.pageContent.introItemsHi.description: Guidance under the list of blocks on an introduction screen.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introItemsLa.description: Label of the ordered list of pieces the introduction screen is built from.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.introTitle.description: Heading of the section where a researcher builds a page of text and media shown before this step of the interview’s own task begins.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageAddLabel.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding one more piece to a page. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because a stage editor shows several lists at once.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageAddTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add one more piece to a page.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageClearCon.description: Action that confirms switching a page off and discarding its blocks.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageClearDes.defaultMessage: This will remove every block on this page. Do you want to continue?
protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageClearDes.description: Body of the confirmation asked before switching a page off, which throws every block on it away.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageClearTit.description: Title of the confirmation asked before switching a page off, which throws every block on it away.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageDescript.defaultMessage: Write the page heading and build the sequence of blocks the participant reads.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageEditTitl.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a piece of a page.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageEmptySta.defaultMessage: No blocks yet. Create one to put text or media on this page.
protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageEmptySta.description: Shown in place of the list of blocks while a page holds nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageItemNoun.description: What one piece of a page is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit block", "Remove this block?" — so it is lower case and singular.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageItemsHin.defaultMessage: The participant scrolls through these in order, so add as many as you need. Drag to reorder them.
protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageItemsHin.description: Guidance under the list of blocks on a page.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageItemsLab.description: Label of the ordered list of pieces a page is built from — passages of text, pictures, videos.

protocolBuilder.pageContent.pageTitle.description: Heading of the section where a researcher builds a page of text and media that a participant reads instead of doing a task.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesChild.defaultMessage: For each of the participant's children, asks that the child's other genetic parent has their own parents and grandparents recorded, extending the family pedigree to that side of the family. Participants without children can affirm this instead.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesChild.description: Guidance under the co-parent family requirement control. "Affirm this instead" means a participant with no children confirms that fact rather than recording anybody.
Label of the control setting how strictly the pedigree asks about the families of the people the participant had children with.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesDescr.defaultMessage: Set how far the pedigree must extend beyond the participant's immediate family.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesDescr.description: Description of the pedigree boundaries section.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesEnfor.defaultMessage: Each boundary below can be set to one of three enforcement levels, which determine how the interview behaves when the condition is not yet met:
protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesEnfor.description: Sentence introducing the list of enforcement levels below it, so it ends in a colon.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesGrand.defaultMessage: Asks the participant to record two parents for each of their own parents, so that all of the participant's grandparents appear in the family pedigree.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesGrand.description: Guidance under the grandparent requirement control.
Label of the control setting how strictly the pedigree asks for the participant’s grandparents.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesLevel.description: Enforcement level meaning the boundary is never checked. Keyed by the schema value "off".
Enforcement level meaning the participant is reminded but may finish anyway. Keyed by the schema value "recommended".
Enforcement level meaning the participant cannot finish the stage until the boundary is met. Keyed by the schema value "required".

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesOffEx.defaultMessage: <term>Off</term> — the condition is never checked, and participants are not asked to provide this information.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesOffEx.description: What the "Off" enforcement level does. The <term> tag holds the level’s own name and is drawn in bold; keep it matching the "Off" option label below.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesRecom.defaultMessage: <term>Recommended</term> — participants see a reminder in the completion checklist, but can finish the stage without satisfying the condition.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesRecom.description: What the "Recommended" enforcement level does. The <term> tag holds the level’s own name and is drawn in bold; keep it matching the "Recommended" option label. The completion checklist is a list the participant sees on the pedigree screen.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesRequi.defaultMessage: <term>Required</term> — participants cannot finish the stage until the condition is satisfied.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesRequi.description: What the "Required" enforcement level does. The <term> tag holds the level’s own name and is drawn in bold; keep it matching the "Required" option label.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesSelec.description: Shown in an enforcement-level control while the researcher has chosen no level yet.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.boundariesTitle.description: Heading of the section setting how far beyond their immediate family a participant has to record before the stage will let them finish.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.censusDescripti.defaultMessage: Write the question the participant answers while they build their family.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.censusDescripti.description: Description of the family-building prompt section.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.censusFieldHint.defaultMessage: Shown throughout the family-building phase, so it should describe the whole task rather than one step of it.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.censusFieldHint.description: Guidance under the census prompt field.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.censusFieldLabe.description: Label of the field holding the question. "Census" is this interface’s name for the phase in which the participant lists everyone in their family.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.censusPlacehold.description: Placeholder shown in the empty census prompt field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.censusTitle.description: Heading of the section holding the single question shown while a participant is drawing their family.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.dependentStages.defaultMessage: These stages visualize this pedigree's network and map their own attributes onto its node type: {stageNames}. Changing the node type here will leave them pointing at attributes the new type does not have.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.dependentStages.description: Body of the warning about other stages that read this pedigree. stageNames is the list of those stages’ names, each in quotation marks, already joined into one phrase in the reader’s language.
Title of the warning shown above the node type control when other stages of the same protocol draw their network from this pedigree.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeDescription.defaultMessage: Choose the edge type and map the attributes used to store family relationships.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeDescription.description: Description of the relationship data section.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGameteRoleC.defaultMessage: Create the categorical attribute the pedigree records gamete roles in
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGameteRoleC.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the gamete role attribute. "The" rather than "a", because only one value set is allowed and the dialog seeds it.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGameteRoleC.defaultMessage: Create a new gamete role attribute
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGameteRoleC.description: Button that opens a dialog for adding the gamete role attribute to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGameteRoleH.defaultMessage: A categorical attribute recording whether a parent contributed the egg or the sperm, which the pedigree traces biological inheritance through. Its values are fixed by the interface.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGameteRoleH.description: Guidance under the gamete role control. "Its values are fixed by the interface" means the researcher may not edit the answers this attribute offers.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGameteRoleL.description: Label of the control binding the attribute that records which reproductive cell a parent contributed — the egg or the sperm.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGestational.defaultMessage: Create a boolean attribute recording who carried each pregnancy
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGestational.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the gestational carrier attribute.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGestational.defaultMessage: Create a new gestational carrier attribute
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGestational.description: Button that opens a dialog for adding the gestational carrier attribute to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGestational.defaultMessage: A boolean attribute recording who carried each pregnancy. It is only written on parent relationships.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeGestational.description: Guidance under the gestational carrier control.
Label of the control binding the attribute that records who carried each pregnancy. A gestational carrier is the person who was pregnant, who may not be a genetic parent.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeIsActiveCre.defaultMessage: Create a boolean attribute recording whether a relationship is current
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeIsActiveCre.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the active status attribute.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeIsActiveCre.defaultMessage: Create a new active status attribute
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeIsActiveCre.description: Button that opens a dialog for adding the active status attribute to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeIsActiveHin.defaultMessage: A boolean attribute recording whether the relationship is a current one.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeIsActiveHin.description: Guidance under the active status control.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeIsActiveLab.description: Label of the control binding the attribute that records whether a relationship is a current one.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeRelationshi.defaultMessage: Create the categorical attribute the pedigree records relationship kinds in
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeRelationshi.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the relationship type attribute. "The" rather than "a", because only one value set is allowed and the dialog seeds it.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeRelationshi.defaultMessage: Create a new relationship type attribute
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeRelationshi.description: Button that opens a dialog for adding the relationship type attribute to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeRelationshi.defaultMessage: A categorical attribute holding what kind of relationship each edge is — biological, social, donor, surrogate, adoptive or partner. Its values are fixed by the interface.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeRelationshi.description: Guidance under the relationship type control. The six words are the kinds of relationship a pedigree can record. "Its values are fixed by the interface" means the researcher may not edit the answers this attribute offers.
Label of the control binding the attribute that holds what kind of relationship each edge is.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeTitle.description: Heading of the section binding the edge type and the attributes the pedigree stores each family relationship’s details in.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeTypeHint.defaultMessage: Every relationship the pedigree records — parents, partners and donors alike — is an edge of this one type.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeTypeHint.description: Guidance under the pedigree’s edge type control.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.edgeTypeLabel.description: Label of the control choosing which edge type of the codebook a family relationship is.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingDescript.defaultMessage: Choose fixed terminology or let each participant select their preferred framing.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingDescript.description: Description of the pedigree framing section. "Framing" is this interface’s name for one of two sets of words it can ask about parents with.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingGamete.description: Name of the framing that describes parents by their reproductive contribution — the egg and the sperm — rather than by gender. Keyed by the schema value "gamete"; the participant-facing words this framing selects live in the interview runtime and are translated there.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingGameteEx.defaultMessage: <term>Gamete-based</term> — describes each parent by their reproductive contribution, using terms such as “egg parent” and “sperm parent” and questions such as “Who provided the egg?”. This framing works for all family structures, including donor conception, surrogacy, and same-sex parents.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingGameteEx.description: What the gamete-based framing does, in the list a researcher chooses a framing from. The <term> tag holds the framing’s own name and is drawn in bold; keep it around whatever names the framing in your language, and keep it matching the "Gamete-based" option label. The quoted phrases are examples of what a participant would read.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingGendered.description: Name of the framing that describes parents with gendered kinship terms — mother, father. Keyed by the schema value "gendered".

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingGendered.defaultMessage: <term>Gendered</term> — uses gendered kinship terms such as “mother” and “father” and questions such as “Who is the biological mother?”. This framing assumes that each child has a mother and a father.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingGendered.description: What the gendered framing does, in the list a researcher chooses a framing from. The <term> tag holds the framing’s own name and is drawn in bold; keep it matching the "Gendered" option label. The quoted phrases are examples of what a participant would read.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingIntro.defaultMessage: The framing determines the language the interface uses when talking about biological parents:
protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingIntro.description: Sentence introducing the list of framings below it, so it ends in a colon. "The interface" is the pedigree screen the participant sees.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingModeFixe.description: Option meaning the researcher chooses one framing and every participant gets it. Keyed by the schema value "fixed".

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingModeLabe.description: Label of the control choosing whether the researcher fixes the framing or the participant picks it.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingModePart.description: Option meaning each participant picks their own framing during the interview. Keyed by the schema value "participantChoice".

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingSharedWo.defaultMessage: Both framings use the same wording for gestational carriers and donors.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingSharedWo.description: Said under the two framing explanations, so a researcher knows the choice does not affect how the pedigree asks about a surrogate or a donor.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingTitle.description: Heading of the section where a researcher chooses the vocabulary the pedigree uses when it asks a participant about biological parents.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.framingValueLab.description: Label of the control naming which framing every participant gets. Shown only while the framing mode is fixed.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormAddLa.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding one more question to the family member form. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because a stage editor shows several lists at once and they would otherwise be indistinguishable to anyone navigating by a list of buttons.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormClear.description: Button that confirms switching off the family member form and discarding it.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormClear.defaultMessage: Every field you have added to it will be removed, and participants will no longer be asked anything when they add a family member.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormClear.description: Body of the confirmation shown before the family member form is switched off, saying what is lost. A field is one question the form asks.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormClear.defaultMessage: This will delete the family member form
protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormClear.description: Title of the confirmation shown before a researcher switches off the form a Family Pedigree asks about each family member. Switching it off discards the form, which is why it is confirmed.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormDescr.defaultMessage: Optionally ask the participant more about each family member as they add them.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormDescr.description: Description of the family member form section. Optional because a pedigree may ask nothing at all about each person.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormEmpty.defaultMessage: No form fields yet. Create one to ask something about each family member.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormEmpty.description: Shown in place of the family member form’s field list while it asks nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormField.defaultMessage: The participant answers these when they add or edit a family member. Drag to reorder them.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormField.description: Guidance under the list of family member form fields.
Label of the ordered list of questions the family member form asks.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.memberFormTitle.description: Heading of the section holding what a Family Pedigree asks about each person the participant adds. Replaces the shared form section’s generic heading, because this form describes a relative rather than standing on its own.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeBiologicalS.defaultMessage: Create the categorical attribute the pedigree records sex in
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeBiologicalS.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the biological sex attribute. "The" rather than "a", because only one value set is allowed and the dialog seeds it.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeBiologicalS.defaultMessage: Create a new biological sex attribute
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeBiologicalS.description: Button that opens a dialog for adding the biological sex attribute to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeBiologicalS.defaultMessage: A categorical attribute holding each family member's sex recorded at birth, which the pedigree traces sex-linked inheritance through. Its values are fixed by the interface.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeBiologicalS.description: Guidance under the biological sex control. "Its values are fixed by the interface" means the researcher may not edit the list of answers this attribute offers, because the genetics engine branches on those exact values.
Label of the control binding the attribute that holds each family member’s sex recorded at birth.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeDescription.defaultMessage: Choose the node type and map the attributes used to represent family members.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeDescription.description: Description of the family member data section. "Map" here means point each of the interface’s slots at one attribute of the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeEgoCreateDe.defaultMessage: Create a boolean attribute marking the participant
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeEgoCreateDe.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the participant identifier attribute.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeEgoCreateLa.defaultMessage: Create a new participant identifier attribute
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeEgoCreateLa.description: Button that opens a dialog for adding the participant identifier attribute to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeEgoHint.defaultMessage: A boolean attribute marking which node is the participant. Every completeness check keys off it, so nothing else may write it.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeEgoHint.description: Guidance under the participant identifier control. A completeness check is one of the boundary rules that decide whether the participant may finish the stage.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeEgoLabel.description: Label of the control binding the attribute that marks which person in the family tree is the participant themselves.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeLabelCreate.defaultMessage: Create a text attribute for family member names
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeLabelCreate.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the display label attribute, so the researcher knows what the attribute they are naming is for.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeLabelCreate.defaultMessage: Create a new display label attribute
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeLabelCreate.description: Button that opens a dialog for adding the display label attribute to the codebook. Whole rather than a generic "Create", because a pedigree editor shows several of these at once and they would otherwise be indistinguishable to anyone navigating by a list of buttons.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeLabelHint.defaultMessage: A text attribute holding the name shown on each family member other than the participant, who is drawn without one.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeLabelHint.description: Guidance under the display label control.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeLabelLabel.description: Label of the control binding the attribute that holds the name shown on each person drawn in the family tree.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeRelationshi.defaultMessage: Create a text attribute for each relationship to the participant
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeRelationshi.description: Said inside the dialog for creating the relationship-to-participant attribute.
Button that opens a dialog for adding the relationship-to-participant attribute to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeRelationshi.defaultMessage: A text attribute holding each person's relationship to the participant, such as mother, uncle, or daughter. The pedigree works this out from the family tree.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeRelationshi.description: Guidance under the relationship-to-participant control. The three examples are kinship terms and should be replaced with natural ones in your language.
Label of the control binding the attribute that holds how each person is related to the participant.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeTitle.description: Heading of the section binding the node type and the attributes the pedigree stores each family member’s details in.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeTypeHint.defaultMessage: Every family member the participant adds will be a node of this type.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeTypeHint.description: Guidance under the pedigree’s node type control.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nodeTypeLabel.description: Label of the control choosing which node type of the codebook a family member is.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationAddLa.description: Button that opens the dialog for writing one more nomination prompt. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because a pedigree editor shows several lists at once and they would otherwise be indistinguishable to anyone navigating by a list of buttons.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationAddTi.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to write one more nomination prompt.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationAtLea.defaultMessage: Add at least one nomination prompt, or switch this section off.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationAtLea.description: Refusal shown above the nomination prompt list when a researcher saves a pedigree whose nomination section is switched on and empty. Switching the section off is the other way out, and is offered beside the list.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationCreat.defaultMessage: Create a boolean attribute for this nomination prompt
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationCreat.description: Said inside the dialog for creating a nomination prompt’s attribute.
Button that opens a dialog for adding the attribute this nomination prompt will record its answers in to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationDescr.defaultMessage: Optionally ask the participant to mark family members who share a condition or trait.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationDescr.description: Description of the nomination prompts section. Optional because a pedigree that only draws the family is a complete pedigree.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationEditT.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a nomination prompt they have already written.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationEmpty.defaultMessage: No nomination prompts yet. Create one to ask the participant to mark family members.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationEmpty.description: Shown in place of the nomination prompt list while the section is switched on but holds nothing.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationField.defaultMessage: The participant answers each of these across the whole family, in this order. Drag to reorder them.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationField.description: Guidance under the list of nomination prompts.
Label of the list of nomination prompts. The same words as the section heading, and translated once for each: the heading names the part of the stage, and this names the control.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationPrevi.description: Stands in for a nomination prompt’s question in the list while the researcher has written none.
Shown on one closed nomination prompt row, saying where its answers go. attributeName is the codebook name the researcher gave that attribute, which is not translated.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationPromp.description: What one row of the nomination prompt list is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit nomination prompt", "Remove this nomination prompt?" — so it is lower case and singular. Qualified rather than plain "prompt" because a pedigree editor shows a census prompt beside it.
Button that confirms switching off the nomination prompts and discarding them.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationPromp.defaultMessage: Every prompt you have written here will be removed, and participants will no longer be asked to mark family members.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationPromp.description: Body of the confirmation shown before the nomination prompts are switched off, saying what is lost. A nomination prompt asks the participant to mark which family members share a condition or trait.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationPromp.defaultMessage: This will delete your nomination prompts
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationPromp.description: Title of the confirmation shown before a researcher switches off a Family Pedigree’s nomination prompts. Switching them off discards them, which is why it is confirmed.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationTextH.defaultMessage: The question the participant answers for each family member.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationTextH.description: Guidance under a nomination prompt’s question field.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationTextL.description: Label of the field holding the question one nomination prompt asks.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationTextP.description: Placeholder shown in a nomination prompt’s empty question field. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationTextR.defaultMessage: Enter the question this prompt asks.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationTextR.description: Refusal shown under a nomination prompt’s question field when the researcher saves the row without writing one.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationTitle.description: Heading of the optional section holding questions the participant answers about the whole family at once, by marking the members each one applies to.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationVaria.defaultMessage: No boolean attributes of this node type can be nominated yet. Create one to continue.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationVaria.description: Shown in place of a nomination prompt’s attribute list when every boolean attribute of the node type is already written by something else.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationVaria.defaultMessage: The boolean attribute each answer is recorded in.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationVaria.description: Guidance under a nomination prompt’s attribute control. Boolean because the participant either marks a family member or does not.
Label of the control choosing which codebook attribute one nomination prompt’s answers are stored in.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationVaria.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute this prompt records.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationVaria.description: Refusal shown under a nomination prompt’s attribute control when the researcher saves the row without choosing one.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationWaiti.defaultMessage: Choose a node type before writing this pedigree’s nomination prompts.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.nominationWaiti.description: Shown in place of the nomination prompts section’s description while the researcher has not yet chosen the node type, so there is no attribute for a prompt to record its answer in.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotDraftFormCo.defaultMessage: "{attributeName}" is collected by this stage’s own form, so it cannot also be written by this slot (values written here would bypass its validation)
protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotDraftFormCo.description: Refusal shown under a pedigree slot the interface writes directly, when the attribute picked is already collected by the family member form one section above — so both are on the screen the researcher is looking at, and the wording must not send them searching their other stages. attributeName is the codebook name of the attribute, which is not translated.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotDraftSlotDe.defaultMessage: "{attributeName}" is written without validation by another slot in this stage, so it cannot also be collected here (the values that slot writes bypass this attribute’s validation)
protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotDraftSlotDe.description: Refusal shown under the display label — the one pedigree slot whose value is collected through a form field — when the attribute picked is already written directly by another slot of the same stage. Deliberately says "slot" rather than "form field": told it cannot be used as a form field, a researcher goes looking for a form field they never added. attributeName is the codebook name of the attribute, which is not translated.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotEmptyState.defaultMessage: No attributes of this type can be used here yet. Create one to continue.
protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotEmptyState.description: Shown in place of a pedigree slot’s attribute list when the codebook offers nothing this slot can take — usually because every candidate is already written by something else. "Of this type" means of the attribute type the slot needs, such as text or boolean.

protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotUnvalidated.defaultMessage: "{attributeName}" is written without validation by another stage, so it cannot also be collected here (the values that stage writes bypass this attribute’s validation)
protocolBuilder.pedigree.slotUnvalidated.description: Refusal shown under a pedigree slot that collects an answer — the display label — when the attribute picked is already written directly by another stage of the protocol, which would let unchecked values in under the same name. attributeName is the codebook name of the attribute, which is not translated.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.addLabel.description: Button that opens the dialog for writing one more question. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because a stage editor shows several lists at once and they would otherwise be indistinguishable to anyone navigating by a list of buttons.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.addTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to write one more question.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.atLeastOn.defaultMessage: Create at least one prompt. A stage with no prompts asks the participant nothing.
protocolBuilder.promptsSection.atLeastOn.description: Refusal shown above the prompt list when a researcher saves a stage that asks nothing. A prompt is one question a participant is asked; a stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.descripti.defaultMessage: Write the questions this stage asks, and drag them into the order the participant answers them.
protocolBuilder.promptsSection.descripti.description: Description of the prompts section. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.editTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a question they have already written.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.emptyStat.defaultMessage: No prompts yet. Create one to say what this stage asks the participant.
protocolBuilder.promptsSection.emptyStat.description: Shown in place of the prompt list while a stage asks nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.fieldHint.defaultMessage: The participant answers these one at a time, in this order. Add at least one.
protocolBuilder.promptsSection.fieldHint.description: Guidance under the list of prompts.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.fieldLabe.description: Label of the list of questions inside the prompts section. The same word as the section heading, and translated once for each: the heading names the part of the stage, and this names the control.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.itemNoun.description: What one row of the prompt list is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit prompt", "Remove this prompt?" — so it is lower case and singular. A prompt is one question a participant is asked.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.title.description: Heading of the section holding the questions this step of the interview asks the participant.

protocolBuilder.promptsSection.waitingDe.defaultMessage: Choose what this stage works with before writing its prompts.
protocolBuilder.promptsSection.waitingDe.description: Shown in place of the prompts section’s description while the researcher has not yet chosen which node or edge type the stage is about, so there is nothing for a prompt to be written against.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.duplicat.description: Why part of the codebook could not be read: two entity types share a name. name is the researcher-authored type name; firstOwnerSectionId identifies the part of the protocol that used it first.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.missingS.defaultMessage: Protocol sections do not include a stage order.
protocolBuilder.protocolContext.missingS.description: Why the interview steps could not be put in order: the protocol has nothing saying what the order is.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageIdM.defaultMessage: Stage document id {documentId} does not match section id {sectionStageId}.
protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageIdM.description: Why one interview step could not be read: the identifier inside it disagrees with the one it is filed under. "stage" is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageMis.defaultMessage: Stage {stageId} is missing from the stage order.
protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageMis.description: Why one interview step is not shown: the protocol has it but the order does not name it. "stage" is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageOrd.defaultMessage: Stage order must not list the same stage twice.
protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageOrd.description: Why the order of the interview steps could not be read: one step appears in it more than once. "stage" is one step of an interview.
Why the order of the interview steps could not be used: it names a step the protocol does not have. "stage" is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageOrd.defaultMessage: Stage order must be a list of non-empty stage ids.
protocolBuilder.protocolContext.stageOrd.description: Why the order of the interview steps could not be read. "stage" is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.unknownS.description: Why part of the protocol could not be read: it is filed under a name this version does not recognise.

protocolBuilder.protocolContext.variable.defaultMessage: Attribute record key "{variableId}" is reused across entity types (first declared in {firstOwnerSectionId}).
protocolBuilder.protocolContext.variable.description: Why part of the codebook could not be read: two entity types store an attribute under the same key. variableId is the key; firstOwnerSectionId identifies the part of the protocol that used it first.

protocolBuilder.protocolField.required.description: Shown under any unanswered required control in a stage editor when the researcher tries to save the stage. Addresses the researcher authoring the protocol, not a participant answering it.

protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.emptySta.defaultMessage: There are no resources to choose from yet.
protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.emptySta.description: Shown in place of the resource list when the protocol holds none of the kind this field accepts and none has been imported yet.

protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.libraryD.defaultMessage: Resources already saved, and anything imported since this stage was opened.
protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.libraryD.description: Description under the heading of the resource list. "Stage" is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.libraryT.description: Heading over the list of resources — images, audio, video, participant data, API keys — a researcher can choose from. Also the accessible name of that list.

protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.loading.description: Shown while the list of a protocol’s resources is being read for the first time.

protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.retryLib.defaultMessage: Try loading the resource list again
protocolBuilder.resourceBrowser.retryLib.description: Button beside a failure notice, which asks the host again for the list of resources. Named rather than generic because several parts of the dialog can be failing at once.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.alreadyC.defaultMessage: that resource is already part of the protocol
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.alreadyC.description: Refusal shown when a save was asked to import a resource the protocol already holds. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.assetVal.description: Fallback reason used when the protocol schema rejected an asset entry without saying why. Appears inside a longer sentence, so it is lower case and has no full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.download.description: Refusal shown when something asked to download an API key’s content. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.fileEmpt.description: Refusal shown when the file a researcher chose holds no bytes at all. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.fileTooL.defaultMessage: the selected file is larger than the {limit, number} byte limit
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.fileTooL.description: Refusal shown when the file a researcher chose exceeds what the host will store. limit is that size as an exact byte count, not a rounded one. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.hostUnav.defaultMessage: the resource host is temporarily unavailable
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.hostUnav.description: Refusal shown when the store holding protocol resources cannot answer right now. Lower case and without a full stop: surfaces put it after a clause of their own.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.invalidM.description: Shown to a researcher when a host proposed a protocol asset entry the protocol schema rejects. resourceId is the asset id; reason is the schema’s own English message, or the generic fallback. Lower case because a surface may put it after a clause of its own.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.invalidR.defaultMessage: The resource ("{resourceId}") this stage uses is not valid: {reason}
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.invalidR.description: Validation problem shown against the field of an interview stage whose resource has an unusable entry in the protocol. resourceId is the asset id; reason is the schema’s own English message, or the generic fallback.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.manifest.defaultMessage: the asset manifest could not be updated
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.manifest.description: Refusal shown when the protocol’s own list of resources could not be written while saving. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.missingR.defaultMessage: This stage uses a resource ("{resourceId}") that is not in the protocol.
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.missingR.description: Validation problem shown against the field of an interview stage (one step of an interview) that names a resource the protocol does not contain. resourceId is the asset id the field holds.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.notFound.defaultMessage: that resource is no longer available
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.notFound.description: Refusal shown when nothing in the protocol or this editing session has the requested resource id. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.previewU.description: Refusal shown when something asked to display an API key’s content. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.defaultMessage: a promotion may name each resource only once
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.description: Refusal shown when a save of imported resources named the same one twice. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.defaultMessage: a promotion requires a stable request id
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.description: Refusal shown when a save of imported resources arrived without the identifier that makes it safe to repeat. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.defaultMessage: a promotion must name at least one staged resource
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.description: Refusal shown when a save of imported resources named none of them. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.defaultMessage: the resources could not be stored; nothing was changed
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.description: Refusal shown when saving a stage’s imported resources failed partway and every part of it was undone. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.defaultMessage: the last attempt to save these resources did not say whether it finished, so they cannot be discarded until saving again settles it
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.promotio.description: Refusal shown when a researcher asks to discard an imported resource whose last save never reported whether it committed. Lower case and without a full stop: surfaces put it after a clause of their own.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.readOnly.defaultMessage: this protocol is open for viewing only, so its resources cannot change
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.readOnly.description: Refusal shown when a researcher tries to import, discard, or save a resource in a protocol opened read-only. Lower case and without a full stop because surfaces put it after a clause of their own.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.resource.defaultMessage: That resource is no longer available: it was discarded while this list was open. Close and reopen the browser to see what there is.
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.resource.description: Refusal shown when a researcher picks a resource from a list read before that resource was discarded. "The browser" is this app’s resource-picking dialog, not the web browser.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.resource.defaultMessage: That resource is being discarded, so it cannot be used here. Choose a different one.
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.resource.description: Refusal shown when a researcher picks a resource another field is in the middle of discarding.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterAt.defaultMessage: the "{name}" attribute cannot be used as a variable name: names may hold only letters, digits, and the characters . _ - :
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterAt.description: Refusal shown when an imported roster carries a column or attribute name a protocol variable cannot take — a spreadsheet heading such as "home address". name is that heading, left exactly as the researcher wrote it. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterEm.defaultMessage: the selected file has no records in it, so a stage using it would have nobody to show
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterEm.description: Refusal shown when an imported roster parsed correctly but holds no entries. "Stage" is one step of an interview. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterNo.defaultMessage: the attributes of node {position} are not an object
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterNo.description: Names the entry at fault in an imported roster whose attributes are malformed. "Node" is one person or entity in network data; position is its one-based place in the file. Lower case and without a full stop.

Names the entry at fault in an imported roster. "Node" is the network-research term for one person or entity in the data; position is its one-based place in the file. Appears after a clause of its own, so it is lower case and has no full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterUn.defaultMessage: the selected file is not a readable network
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterUn.description: Refusal shown when an imported roster (participant data an interview reads) cannot be parsed as network data. "Network" is the network-research sense: people and the ties between them. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterUn.defaultMessage: the selected file is not a readable network: {detail}
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterUn.description: The same refusal as rosterUnreadable, with the specific fault named. detail is one of the roster* messages below, already localized. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterVa.defaultMessage: the "{name}" attribute of node {position} is not a value a variable can hold
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterVa.description: Names the attribute at fault in an imported JSON roster. name is the researcher’s own attribute name; "node" is one person or entity in network data and position is its one-based place in the file. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterVa.defaultMessage: the "{name}" attribute of row {row} is not a value a variable can hold
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.rosterVa.description: Names the cell at fault in an imported spreadsheet roster. name is the researcher’s own column heading; row is its one-based line in the file. "Attribute" and "variable" are the data fields a protocol records. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.saveInFl.defaultMessage: these resources are being saved right now, so they cannot be discarded until the save finishes
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.saveInFl.description: Refusal shown when a researcher asks to discard an imported resource while the stage that uses it is being saved. Lower case and without a full stop: surfaces put it after a clause of their own.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.secretNe.defaultMessage: a staged secret can only be promoted with its staged handle
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.secretNe.description: Refusal shown when a save tried to store an API key without the token the host issued for it. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.secretNe.defaultMessage: a staged secret needs a stable request id and a name
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.secretNe.description: Refusal shown when an API key was submitted without the name or request identifier the host needs. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.secretVa.description: Refusal shown when an API key was submitted with no value in it. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.sessionC.defaultMessage: this stage was discarded, so its resources can no longer be saved
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.sessionC.description: Refusal shown when a save is attempted after the interview stage being edited was discarded. "Stage" is one step of an interview. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.stagingE.defaultMessage: this editing session ended before the file finished staging, so it was not kept
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.stagingE.description: Refusal shown when a researcher’s imported file finished uploading after they had already discarded or saved the stage. Lower case and without a full stop: surfaces put it after a clause of their own.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.stagingE.defaultMessage: this editing session ended before the secret finished staging, so it was not kept
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.stagingE.description: Refusal shown when a researcher’s API key finished being stored after they had already discarded or saved the stage. Lower case and without a full stop: surfaces put it after a clause of their own.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.unreacha.defaultMessage: The resource could not be reached. Try again in a moment.
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.unreacha.description: Shown to a researcher when the host storing protocol resources (images, audio, rosters, API keys) threw instead of answering. Deliberately says nothing about the host.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.unsavabl.defaultMessage: The resource ("{resourceId}") this stage uses cannot be saved: {reason}
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.unsavabl.description: Validation problem shown when saving an interview stage and the host will not vouch for a resource it references. resourceId is the asset id; reason is the host’s own refusal, itself a localized sentence.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.uploadNe.defaultMessage: a staged file needs a filename without path separators
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.uploadNe.description: Refusal shown when an imported file’s recorded filename still carries a folder path. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.uploadNe.defaultMessage: a staged file needs a stable request id and a name
protocolBuilder.resourceFailure.uploadNe.description: Refusal shown when an imported file arrived without the name or request identifier the host needs. Lower case and without a full stop.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.apikeyBrow.defaultMessage: Add an API key, or choose one already stored in this protocol.
protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.apikeyBrow.description: Description under the title of the dialog where a researcher picks or adds an API key.
Title of the dialog where a researcher picks or adds an API key.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.apikeyChan.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that already holds an API key.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.apikeyImpo.description: Heading over the form for adding a new API key inside the resource dialog.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.apikeyLabe.description: Name of the resource type that holds a map provider’s API key. Shown as a badge beside a resource in a protocol’s resource list.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.apikeySele.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that holds a map provider’s API key, when the field holds none yet.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.audioBrows.defaultMessage: Import an audio file, or choose one already stored in this protocol.
protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.audioBrows.description: Description under the title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports an audio file.
Title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports an audio file.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.audioChang.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that already holds an audio file.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.audioImpor.description: Heading over the file-import area for audio inside the resource dialog.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.audioLabel.description: Name of the resource type that holds an audio recording. Shown as a badge beside a resource in a protocol’s resource list.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.audioSelec.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that holds an audio file, when the field holds none yet.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.byteLength.description: A resource’s stored size when it is under one kilobyte. size is the exact byte count.
A resource’s stored size in kilobytes, always to one decimal place. size is that already-rounded number; KB is the unit symbol.
A resource’s stored size in megabytes, always to one decimal place. size is that already-rounded number; MB is the unit symbol.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.committedS.description: Badge on a resource the protocol already contains, as opposed to one imported but not yet saved.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.fileBrowse.defaultMessage: Import a file, or choose a resource already stored in this protocol.
protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.fileBrowse.description: Description under the title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports a resource of any kind.
Title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports a resource of any kind.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.fileChange.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that accepts any kind of resource and already holds one.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.fileImport.description: Heading over the file-import area for any kind of file inside the resource dialog.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.fileSelect.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that accepts any kind of resource, when the field holds none yet.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.geojsonBro.defaultMessage: Import a GeoJSON map layer, or choose one already stored in this protocol.
protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.geojsonBro.description: Description under the title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports a GeoJSON map layer.
Title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports a GeoJSON map layer.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.geojsonCha.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that already holds a GeoJSON map layer.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.geojsonImp.description: Heading over the file-import area for map layers inside the resource dialog.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.geojsonLab.description: Name of the resource type that holds a GeoJSON map layer. Shown as a badge beside a resource in a protocol’s resource list.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.geojsonSel.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that holds a GeoJSON map layer, when the field holds none yet.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.imageBrows.defaultMessage: Import an image, or choose one already stored in this protocol.
protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.imageBrows.description: Description under the title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports an image.
Title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports an image.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.imageChang.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that already holds an image.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.imageImpor.description: Heading over the file-import area for images inside the resource dialog.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.imageLabel.description: Name of the resource type that holds a picture. Shown as a badge beside a resource in a protocol’s resource list.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.imageSelec.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that holds an image, when the field holds none yet.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.networkBro.defaultMessage: Import a CSV or JSON data file, or choose one already stored in this protocol.
protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.networkBro.description: Description under the title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports participant data (a roster). CSV and JSON are file formats and stay untranslated.
Title of the dialog where a researcher picks or imports participant data (a roster).

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.networkCha.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that already holds imported participant data.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.networkImp.description: Heading over the file-import area for participant data inside the resource dialog.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.networkLab.description: Name of the resource type that holds imported participant data — a roster of people and the ties between them, in the network-research sense. Shown as a badge beside a resource in a protocol’s resource list.

protocolBuilder.resourceKinds.networkSel.description: Button that opens the picker for a stage field that holds imported participant data, when the field holds none yet.
