protocolBuilder.shell.formUnavailableRef.description: Shown above a stage editor’s fields when a save arrives after the editor’s own form has been taken down, so there are no values left to save.

protocolBuilder.shell.readOnlyRefusal.defaultMessage: This stage is read-only, so your changes were not saved. Take over editing and try again.
protocolBuilder.shell.readOnlyRefusal.description: Shown above a stage editor’s fields when the researcher no longer holds the right to edit this stage (a stage is one step of an interview) and something they did would have written to it. Taking over editing is an action offered elsewhere in the host application.

protocolBuilder.shell.saveFailedRefusal.defaultMessage: This stage could not be saved. Wait a moment and try again.
protocolBuilder.shell.saveFailedRefusal.description: Shown above a stage editor’s fields when saving failed for a reason that carried no explanation of its own. The last resort, used only when the failure said nothing readable.

protocolBuilder.shell.saveStage.description: Action that saves the step of the interview a researcher is editing. Names the stage rather than saying only "Save", because a host may show its own controls beside this one.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.actionHint.defaultMessage: What should happen when the rules match?
protocolBuilder.skipLogic.actionHint.description: Guidance under the control where a researcher says what skip logic does when its rules match.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.actionLabel.description: Label of the control where a researcher says what skip logic does when its rules match: show the stage, or skip it.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.clearConfirm.description: Action that confirms switching skip logic off and discarding its rules.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.clearDescripti.defaultMessage: This will clear your skip logic, and delete any rules you have created. Do you want to continue?
protocolBuilder.skipLogic.clearDescripti.description: Body of the confirmation asked before switching skip logic off, which throws away every rule in it.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.clearTitle.defaultMessage: This will clear your skip logic
protocolBuilder.skipLogic.clearTitle.description: Title of the confirmation asked before switching skip logic off, which throws away every rule in it.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.description.defaultMessage: Determine whether this stage is shown, and where the interview continues when it is skipped.
protocolBuilder.skipLogic.description.description: Description of the skip-logic section. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.destinationHin.defaultMessage: Choose where the interview should continue. Only later stages can be selected.
protocolBuilder.skipLogic.destinationHin.description: Guidance under the control where a researcher chooses where the interview carries on after this step is passed over. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.destinationLab.description: Label of the control where a researcher chooses where the interview carries on after this step is passed over.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.rulesHint.defaultMessage: Create one or more rules to determine when the action should occur.
protocolBuilder.skipLogic.rulesHint.description: Guidance under the rule builder inside the skip-logic section.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.rulesLabel.description: Label of the rule builder inside the skip-logic section, where a researcher writes the rules that decide whether the stage runs.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.showAction.description: Choice offered to a researcher: when the skip-logic rules match, this step of the interview runs.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.skipAction.description: Choice offered to a researcher: when the skip-logic rules match, this step of the interview is passed over.

protocolBuilder.skipLogic.title.description: Heading of the section where a researcher decides whether one step of an interview runs at all.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.del.defaultMessage: A stage that is no longer in this interview
protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.del.description: Shown as the current, unselectable choice when the stage a skip pointed at has been deleted, so there is no name left to show for it.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.ear.defaultMessage: The stage this skips to no longer comes after this one. Choose a later stage, or end the interview.
protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.ear.description: Shown beside the destination control when the stage a skip pointed at has been moved to before this one, so the interview can no longer reach it by skipping forward.

Shown as the current, unselectable choice when the stage a skip pointed at still exists but has moved to before this one, so the interview can no longer reach it by skipping forward. stageLabel is the researcher’s own name for that stage and is not translated.
The same unselectable choice as earlierStageOption, for a stage the researcher has not named yet, so there is no name to show.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.fin.description: Destination offered when a researcher says where an interview continues after a stage is skipped: it does not continue — the interview finishes there.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.mis.defaultMessage: The stage this skips to is no longer part of this interview. Choose where the interview should continue instead.
protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.mis.description: Shown beside the destination control when the stage a skip pointed at has been deleted from the interview. Addressed to the researcher authoring the protocol.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.nex.description: The default destination offered when a researcher says where an interview continues after a stage is skipped: whichever stage comes next and is not itself skipped. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.sta.description: One stage offered as the destination an interview continues at. position is where that stage will sit in the finished interview, counting from one; stageLabel is the researcher’s own name for it and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.una.defaultMessage: A destination that is no longer available
protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.una.description: Shown as the current, unselectable choice when the stage’s stored destination is one this control can no longer offer and cannot describe more precisely than this.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.unr.defaultMessage: A destination this editor cannot read
protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.unr.description: Shown as the current, unselectable choice when the stage records a destination in a shape the protocol will not accept — a hand-edit or a merge left it there. Nothing is known about where it pointed, so it is named for what is wrong with it.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.unr.defaultMessage: The stage this skips to cannot be read. Choose where the interview should continue instead.
protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.unr.description: Shown beside the destination control when the stage records a destination in a shape the protocol will not accept, so nothing can be said about where it pointed.

protocolBuilder.skipLogicDestination.unt.description: The same offered destination as stageOption, for a stage the researcher has not named yet, so there is no name to show. position is where that stage will sit in the finished interview, counting from one.

protocolBuilder.sortOrder.ascending.description: Direction offered for one sort rule: lowest or earliest first.

protocolBuilder.sortOrder.descending.description: Direction offered for one sort rule: highest or latest first.

protocolBuilder.sortOrder.directionLabel.description: Visible text and accessible name of the column of a sort rule that chooses whether it sorts ascending or descending.

protocolBuilder.sortOrder.missingPropert.defaultMessage: {property} — this attribute is no longer in the codebook
protocolBuilder.sortOrder.missingPropert.description: Label of the only choice left standing for a sort rule that names an attribute a collaborator has since deleted. property is the attribute’s stored record id, which the researcher never chose and which is all that is left of it. Rendered inside a plain dropdown option, which can carry no styling, so the explanation is part of the label.

protocolBuilder.sortOrder.missingPropert.defaultMessage: This rule points at an attribute no longer in the codebook. Choose another or delete the rule.
protocolBuilder.sortOrder.missingPropert.description: Shown above a prompt’s sort rules when one of them names an attribute that has been deleted from the codebook — the protocol’s definition of what an interview records. Names both ways out, because the rule looks complete and is not.

protocolBuilder.sortOrder.originalOrder.description: The choice a sort rule offers for "leave these in the order they already have" — the order network members were placed in, or the order a data file lists them in. Written as an asterisk because that is the value the protocol stores and the shorthand researchers already read in Architect; a language that has a better one-character shorthand may use it.

protocolBuilder.sortOrder.propertyLabel.description: Visible text and accessible name of the column of a sort rule that chooses what the rule sorts by — an attribute of the node, or one of the orders the interview itself can supply.

protocolBuilder.stageName.documentation.description: Link to the documentation for this type of interview interface.

protocolBuilder.stageName.name.description: Section heading and accessible field label for the researcher-authored stage name.

protocolBuilder.stageName.placeholder.description: Placeholder for the researcher-authored stage name field.

protocolBuilder.stageName.position.description: The current stage position in the interview. index is one-based.

protocolBuilder.stageTypeImage.preview.description: Alternative text for a screenshot of an interview interface. interfaceName is the localized interface name, or an unchanged identifier for an unknown future interface.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.edgeCreat.defaultMessage: Create an edge type and use it on this stage
protocolBuilder.subjectSection.edgeCreat.description: Description shown inside the dialog for inventing a kind of relationship, and what the change is called in the record a host keeps of protocol edits.
Button that opens an editor for inventing a kind of relationship without leaving the stage being configured. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.edgeDescr.defaultMessage: Choose the type of edge this stage works with.
protocolBuilder.subjectSection.edgeDescr.description: Description of the edge-type section. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.edgeField.defaultMessage: Every edge this stage creates or shows will be of the type you choose here.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.edgeField.description: Label of the control choosing which kind of relationship this step of the interview is about. The same words as the section heading, and translated once for each.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.edgeTitle.description: Heading of the section where a researcher says which kind of relationship this step of the interview is about. An edge is a connection between two members of the network.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.nodeCreat.defaultMessage: Create a node type and use it on this stage
protocolBuilder.subjectSection.nodeCreat.description: Description shown inside the dialog for inventing a kind of network member, and what the change is called in the record a host keeps of protocol edits.
Button that opens an editor for inventing a kind of network member without leaving the stage being configured. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.nodeDescr.defaultMessage: Choose the type of node this stage works with.
protocolBuilder.subjectSection.nodeDescr.description: Description of the node-type section. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.nodeField.defaultMessage: Every node this stage creates or shows will be of the type you choose here.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.nodeField.description: Label of the control choosing which kind of network member this step of the interview is about. The same words as the section heading, and translated once for each: the heading names the part of the stage, and this names the control.

protocolBuilder.subjectSection.nodeTitle.description: Heading of the section where a researcher says which kind of network member this step of the interview is about. A node is one member of the network a participant describes.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.after.defaultMessage: How far forward from the anchor the participant can choose. Left empty, {days, number} days.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.after.description: Guidance under the days-after field. days is the number of days the interview assumes when the researcher writes none.
Label of the field holding how many days after the anchor date a participant may choose.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.ancho.defaultMessage: The date the window is measured from. Leave it empty to measure from the date of the interview.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.ancho.description: Guidance under the anchor-date field, saying what leaving it empty means.
Label of the field holding the date a relative date picker measures its window from.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.befor.defaultMessage: How far back from the anchor the participant can choose. Left empty, {days, number} days.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.befor.description: Guidance under the days-before field. days is the number of days the interview assumes when the researcher writes none.
Label of the field holding how many days before the anchor date a participant may choose.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.bound.defaultMessage: The earliest and latest dates were cleared, because they were set at the previous resolution. Set them again if you still need them.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.bound.description: Announcement made after the researcher changes how precise a date this field collects, which throws away the earliest and latest dates because they were stored at the old precision.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.maxHi.defaultMessage: The latest date the participant can choose. Left empty, the picker ends on the date of the interview.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.maxHi.description: Guidance under the latest-date field, saying what leaving it empty means.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.maxLa.description: Label of the field holding the latest date a participant may choose.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.maxLa.defaultMessage: Shown at the high end of the scale.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.maxLa.description: Guidance under the field naming the high end of a sliding scale.
Label of the field naming the high end of a sliding scale the participant answers on.
Example wording shown in the empty field naming the high end of a sliding scale. An example a researcher might write about closeness between people, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.maxLa.defaultMessage: Write what the high end of the scale means.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.maxLa.description: Refusal shown under the field naming the high end of a sliding scale when the researcher has left it empty.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.minHi.defaultMessage: The earliest date the participant can choose. Left empty, the picker starts in 1920.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.minHi.description: Guidance under the earliest-date field, saying what leaving it empty means. 1920 is the year the date picker falls back to and is not a translated word.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.minLa.description: Label of the field holding the earliest date a participant may choose.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.minLa.defaultMessage: Shown at the low end of the scale, so the participant knows what the two ends mean.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.minLa.description: Guidance under the field naming the low end of a sliding scale.
Label of the field naming the low end of a sliding scale the participant answers on.
Example wording shown in the empty field naming the low end of a sliding scale. An example a researcher might write about closeness between people, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.minLa.defaultMessage: Write what the low end of the scale means.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.minLa.description: Refusal shown under the field naming the low end of a sliding scale when the researcher has left it empty. The participant sees this wording at one end of the scale, so a scale with no such words is a line with nothing at either end of it.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.resol.description: Choice offered for how precise a date a field collects: a whole calendar date. The bracketed pattern is the literal format the protocol stores and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.variableParameters.resol.defaultMessage: How precise a date this field collects. Changing it clears the earliest and latest dates, because those are stored at the resolution chosen here.
protocolBuilder.variableParameters.resol.description: Guidance under the date-resolution control, warning that changing it throws the two bounds away.
Label of the control choosing how precise a date this field collects.
Choice offered for how precise a date a field collects: a month within a year. The bracketed pattern is the literal format the protocol stores and is not translated.
Choice offered for how precise a date a field collects: a year on its own. The bracketed pattern is the literal format the protocol stores and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.attribute.description: Accessible name of the badge stating what kind of answer the chosen attribute records. attributeType is a protocol schema token such as "number", "text" or "categorical", and is shown as it is stored rather than translated. Read as a label and its value, not as a sentence.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.createAct.description: Button that adds the attribute named in the box beside it to the codebook and selects it.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.createHin.defaultMessage: Adds it to this type’s codebook and selects it above.
protocolBuilder.variablePicker.createHin.description: Guidance under the box for naming a new attribute, saying that it lands in the codebook — the protocol’s definition of what an interview records — and becomes the choice made above.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.createLab.description: Label of the box where a researcher types the name of an attribute that does not exist yet, beside the list of the ones that do. An attribute is one thing an interview records about a network member.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.createPla.description: Example attribute name shown in the empty box. A name the codebook would accept: letters, digits and the symbols . _ - : only, so it deliberately has no space in it. Translate it to an equally valid example if that reads better.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.emptyStat.defaultMessage: No attributes are available to choose from.
protocolBuilder.variablePicker.emptyStat.description: Shown in place of the select when nothing can be picked — the caller offered no attributes at all. An attribute is a variable the protocol’s codebook defines. Callers that can say something more specific pass their own sentence instead.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.missingAt.defaultMessage: This attribute is no longer in the codebook. Choose another one.
protocolBuilder.variablePicker.missingAt.description: Shown under the select when the attribute a researcher’s stored choice names has been deleted from the protocol’s codebook, so the choice has to be made again.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.missingOp.defaultMessage: {attributeId} — this attribute is no longer in the codebook
protocolBuilder.variablePicker.missingOp.description: Name of the one option standing for an attribute the protocol’s codebook no longer defines. attributeId is the raw stored identifier — there is no name left to show, because the definition it would have come from has been deleted.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.placehold.description: Placeholder in the select a researcher chooses one codebook attribute from, shown while nothing has been chosen. An attribute is a variable the protocol’s codebook defines for a node type, an edge type or the interview participant.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.unusableA.defaultMessage: This attribute cannot be used in a rule. Choose another one.
protocolBuilder.variablePicker.unusableA.description: Shown under the select when the attribute a researcher’s stored choice names is still in the codebook but cannot carry a rule. Worded apart from the deleted-attribute sentence on purpose: this attribute is still where the researcher left it.

protocolBuilder.variablePicker.unusableO.defaultMessage: {attributeName} — cannot be used in a rule
protocolBuilder.variablePicker.unusableO.description: Name of the one option standing for an attribute that is still in the protocol’s codebook and still cannot carry a rule, such as one answered with a map position. attributeName is the researcher’s own name for it, from the codebook, and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.attri.defaultMessage: The attribute no longer exists in this entity.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.attri.description: Why the validation rules in front of the researcher cannot be saved: the attribute they belong to has been deleted from the codebook.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.attri.defaultMessage: The latest entity data no longer contains this attribute.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.attri.description: Shown in place of the validation rules when the attribute they belong to has been deleted from the codebook.
Heading of the alert shown in place of the rules when the attribute they belong to has been deleted from the codebook.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.await.description: The submit button after the validation rules have been accepted, while the application finishes writing them back into the protocol.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.compa.description: Heading over the validation rules that judge this attribute’s answer against another attribute’s. "Attribute" is a codebook variable.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.delet.description: Entry standing in for the attribute a comparison rule points at after it has been deleted from the codebook, so the researcher can see what the rule still refers to. id is that attribute’s stored record id.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.descr.defaultMessage: Configure requirements, limits, and comparisons for this attribute.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.descr.description: Sentence under the heading naming the three groups of validation rules the surface offers. "Attribute" is a codebook variable.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.diffe.description: Name of the validation rule requiring this attribute’s answer to differ from another attribute’s. The attribute compared against is chosen in a control beneath.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.draft.defaultMessage: "{variableName}" is assigned without validation by a prompt in this stage, so it cannot be used as a form field
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.draft.description: The same refusal as unvalidatedElsewhere, when the writer without validation is a prompt in the stage being edited. variableName is the researcher’s own name for the attribute. A prompt is the question a participant reads.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.draft.defaultMessage: "{variableName}" is collected by this stage's form, so it cannot be assigned by this prompt (values assigned here would bypass its validation)
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.draft.description: The same refusal as validatedElsewhere, when the form doing the collecting belongs to the stage being edited. variableName is the researcher’s own name for the attribute. A prompt is the question a participant reads.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.failu.description: Heading of the alert shown when saving an attribute’s validation rules was refused. The reason follows underneath.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.great.description: Name of the validation rule requiring this attribute’s answer to be no smaller than another attribute’s. The attribute compared against is chosen in a control beneath.
Name of the validation rule requiring this attribute’s answer to be larger than another attribute’s. The attribute compared against is chosen in a control beneath.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.incom.defaultMessage: Choose a comparison attribute for "{label}", or switch the rule off.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.incom.description: Refusal shown when a rule comparing this attribute against another one has been switched on without saying which. label is that rule’s own name, already translated.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.incom.defaultMessage: Enter a value for "{label}", or switch the rule off.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.incom.description: Refusal shown when a rule that needs a number has been switched on without one. label is that rule’s own name, already translated.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.lessT.description: Name of the validation rule requiring this attribute’s answer to be no larger than another attribute’s. The attribute compared against is chosen in a control beneath.
Name of the validation rule requiring this attribute’s answer to be smaller than another attribute’s. The attribute compared against is chosen in a control beneath.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.limit.description: Heading over the validation rules that bound an answer by a number the researcher types — a length, a value, or how many options may be chosen.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.maxLe.description: Name of the validation rule setting the most characters an answer may have.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.maxSe.description: Name of the validation rule setting the most options a participant may choose.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.maxVa.description: Name of the validation rule setting the largest number an answer may be.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.minLe.description: Name of the validation rule setting the fewest characters an answer may have.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.minSe.description: Name of the validation rule setting the fewest options a participant must choose.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.minVa.description: Name of the validation rule setting the smallest number an answer may be.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.missi.defaultMessage: The selected comparison attribute no longer exists.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.missi.description: Why a validation rule cannot be saved: it compares this attribute against another one that has since been deleted from the codebook. "Attribute" is a codebook variable.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.noCom.defaultMessage: No compatible attribute can satisfy this comparison.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.noCom.description: Shown beneath a comparison rule the researcher cannot switch on, because no other attribute of the same kind could satisfy it without contradicting the rules already set. "Attribute" is a codebook variable.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.requi.description: Name of the validation rule that refuses an answer left blank. Shown as the label of the checkbox that turns the rule on.
Heading over the validation rules that say an answer must be given at all, rather than what it may contain.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.ruleF.description: Refusal shown when a counting rule was given a number below what it allows. rule is the schema’s own name for the rule, such as maxSelected, and is not translated; floor is the smallest number it accepts.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.sameA.description: Name of the validation rule requiring this attribute’s answer to match another attribute’s. The attribute compared against is chosen in a control beneath.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.selec.description: The unchosen entry of the control naming which other attribute a comparison rule judges this one against.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.stale.defaultMessage: Your validation draft has been kept. Saving will apply it to the latest authoritative entity data.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.stale.description: What happens next after the protocol’s codebook changed elsewhere while this validation surface was open.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.submi.description: Button that saves the rules an answer to this attribute must satisfy.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.title.description: Heading of the surface where a researcher sets the rules an answer to one attribute must satisfy. name is the researcher’s own name for that attribute.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.typeC.defaultMessage: The attribute type changed while this validation draft was open. Your draft is still visible, but it cannot be saved. Close and reopen this editor to configure validation for the new attribute type.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.typeC.description: The same refusal as typeChangedIssue, said at length in the warning above the rules, with what to do about it.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.typeC.defaultMessage: The attribute type changed while this validation draft was open.
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.typeC.description: Why the validation rules in front of the researcher cannot be saved: the kind of answer the attribute records was changed elsewhere, and these rules were written for the old one.
Heading of the warning shown when someone else changed what kind of answer this attribute records while its validation was being edited.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.uniqu.description: Name of the validation rule that refuses an answer another network member has already given for this attribute.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.unval.defaultMessage: "{variableName}" is written without validation by another stage, so it cannot be used as a form field
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.unval.description: Refusal shown when a form field picks an attribute that another stage already writes without checking it. variableName is the researcher’s own name for the attribute. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.valid.defaultMessage: "{variableName}" is collected by a form elsewhere in this protocol, so it cannot be written by this stage (values written here would bypass its validation)
protocolBuilder.variableValidation.valid.description: Refusal shown when a stage that writes an attribute without checking it picks one that a form elsewhere in the protocol collects with validation. variableName is the researcher’s own name for the attribute. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.variableValidation.whole.description: Refusal shown when a rule counting characters or choices was given a fraction. rule is the schema’s own name for the rule, such as minValue, and is not translated.
